look_here_first: VASEYGRASS: on ONE intact flowering culm count many slender one-sided racemes (commonly 10–20), then measure ripe paired silky-edged spikelets (~2–2.8 mm). At the INNER leaf collar check a 3–5 mm membranous ligule. The lower glume is absent; the thin hairy upper glume and sterile lemma enclose a smaller firm fertile lemma. Dallisgrass overlaps in head shape but usually has fewer racemes and larger (~2.7–3.9 mm) spikelets. Without a measured mature spikelet and true collar, retain a provisional identification.

crew_field_steps: Trace the single central flowerhead axis and the many narrow racemes spreading in different directions; the installed photo shows this architecture clearly.
Recognize that each slender raceme carries rows of tiny spikelets along one side; the individual hairs are not resolvable in the wide view.
Collect base/ligule, a measured spikelet and the FULL head to distinguish dallisgrass; a distant photograph alone is only a vaseygrass candidate.

One ENTIRE panicle with every raceme attachment visible.
Macro of pairwise spikelets next to millimeter scale and silky margin hairs.
True membranous ligule at blade/sheath junction; compare dallisgrass.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Count branches on ONE complete culm, not overlapping heads. Contrast 2–3 mm spikelets under measured macro with 3–4 mm long-haired dallisgrass; do not key solely by abundance of racemes or overall height. Use Florida paspalum as another few-branch, large-spikelet look-alike.
do_not_use_alone: Number of racemes without the entire flowering axis
Habitat, height, or vegetative tuft in isolation
Microscopic glume hairs or spikelet length inferred from a photo without scale

species_anatomy_finalization_20261024.look_here_first: On ONE intact tall flowering culm, count the many slender one-sided racemes; then examine a mature paired spikelet with a 1-mm scale. A 2–2.8 mm, silky-edged spikelet with NO lower glume supports vaseygrass. Confirm the 3–5 mm membranous true ligule at the INNER blade–sheath junction; do not mistake basal sheath hairs for the ligule.
measured_structures: GROWTH: robust, tufted perennial; culms 80–250 cm in Kew GrassBase; basal leaf sheaths may be hairy. Rooted growth form is not confirmed by the existing wide seedhead photograph.
FLOWERING AXIS: commonly 10–20 unilateral racemes, each about 4–13 cm, distributed along a central axis about 10–20 cm; branches and spikelet rows must be counted on one connected inflorescence.

SPIKELETS: paired, ovate and dorsally compressed, 2–2.8 mm long in Kew; VicFlora includes 1.6–2.8 mm. One basal sterile floret and one upper fertile floret occur within each spikelet; the two adjacent spikelets are NOT two florets.
LOWER GLUME: absent or extremely reduced. Do not draw an arrow to an invented lower glume.
UPPER GLUME: approximately spikelet-length, thin, usually 3-veined (VicFlora permits 3–5), with conspicuous silky cilia on its margins and some surface hairs.
LOWER STERILE LEMMA: approximately spikelet-length, thin, generally 3-veined, often with silky marginal hairs; distinguish this actual lemma from the upper glume in a dissected mature spikelet.

UPPER FERTILE LEMMA: firm/hardened, pale, finely striate, rounded/obtuse at tip; 1.4–2.6 mm in AusGrass, versus 1.6–1.8 mm in Flora of New Zealand. The corresponding palea is firm and enclosed by the incurved lemma margins.
AWNS: no long projecting glume or fertile-lemma awn. Silky marginal hairs are NOT awns.
TRUE LIGULE: unfringed membranous tongue, about 3–5 mm in Kew GrassBase and 3–9 mm in VicFlora; inspect the inner collar separately from adjacent sheath-mouth hairs.
crew_sequence: 1. Photograph a rooted tuft with a complete, connected flowering culm; record the basal sheath hair pattern and any actual rhizome without inferring underground structures.
2. Count all unilateral racemes on that SAME panicle; do not sum several crossing seedheads.
3. Open the inner leaf collar and measure the free membranous ligule with a millimeter ruler; distinguish separate long basal sheath hairs.
4. At 10–20× photograph at least five ripe attached paired spikelets with a 1-mm scale; check the 2–2.8 mm range, shape and silky margin.
5. Dissect one ripe spikelet: identify absent lower glume, thin hairy upper glume, lower sterile lemma, hard upper fertile lemma and palea; mark each only if the pixels actually resolve it.
6. Compare with dallisgrass on the SAME scale: P. dilatatum generally has fewer racemes and larger 2.7–3.9 mm spikelets; size and branch counts overlap, so use multiple traits.
7. If spikelet parts and same-plant collar cannot be verified, retain Paspalum cf. urvillei rather than asserting a confirmed species ID.
local_lookalikes: Paspalum dilatatum (introduced dallisgrass): commonly fewer flowering racemes, spikelets typically 2.7–3.9 mm in AusGrass; silky upper-glume margins also occur, so hairs alone do NOT separate them.
Paspalum pubiflorum: also paired oval spikelets and several unilateral racemes; compare mature upper-glume hairs/veins, branch count and true collar rather than a single close-up row.
Sorghum halepense (introduced Johnsongrass): a branched open panicle with different paired sessile/pedicelled spikelet architecture, NOT the narrow unilateral rows of paired Paspalum spikelets.
needs_public_photo: ROOTED HABIT: source-verified vaseygrass with one connected root crown, basal sheaths and full mature flowering axis, centimeter ruler; avoid treating an isolated seedhead as evidence of perennial base.
TRUE LIGULE: same plant, inner blade–sheath junction opened, side lighting and 1-mm scale; show 3–5 mm membrane separately from basal hairs.
ATTACHED PAIRS: 10–20× ripe spikelets on one raceme, 1-mm scale, silk fringe and pairing resolvable.
DISSECTED PARTS: 20–40× upper glume (including veins), sterile lemma, hard fertile lemma and palea from one vouchered mature spikelet, mm scale; no invented lower-glume or awn arrows.
LOOK-ALIKE: P. dilatatum mature spikelets and intact head photographed at the same scale and orientation; optionally P. pubiflorum.
needs_site_qa: Confirm all existing species JPEG paths physically exist and are rendered in the ordinary public learner; distinguish locally archived bytes from remote references.
Recheck each photograph's exact photographer, source URL, per-photo CC terms and attribution before claiming public-ready.
Inspect existing gross-structure arrows and original photographer's printed anatomy labels against actual pixels; do not claim unmeasured spikelet size or create speculative glume/lemma arrows.
Verify the public card displays LOOK HERE FIRST, anatomy distinctions and remaining photo holds; no Pages/deployment claim until independently checked.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — MANY ONE-SIDED RACEMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: On ONE complete flowering culm, count often 10–20 slender unilateral racemes.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Vaseygrass is a robust perennial bunchgrass; published culms about 80–250 cm. Racemes usually radiate or droop along an elongated axis, but counts overlap dallisgrass. Panel 1 shows the flowering architecture; no connected rooted Texas voucher is shown. Count branches on a single attached panicle, not overlapping heads.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL HEAD PHOTO — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO CONNECTED ROOTED PLANT

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · TRUE MEMBRANOUS LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Open the INNER blade–sheath collar: true membrane often 3–5 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published ligule ranges vary by flora, reaching about 3–9 mm in VicFlora. Separate the free triangular membrane from conspicuous hairs on the lower sheath or stem node. The hairy-node panel is NOT a ligule photograph. Obtain a same-plant opened collar with a millimeter scale before drawing a ligule arrow.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · PAIRED RIPE SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Paired, dorsally flattened spikelets usually about 2–2.8 mm long.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Each small oval spikelet contains one lower sterile and one upper fertile floret; two adjacent spikelets are NOT two florets. Inspect at least five ripe pairs on the same raceme at 10–20× with a 1-mm ruler. Panel 3 shows actual attached spikelets but does not independently establish their size.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL SPIKELET PHOTO — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO CALIBRATED PAIRS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · GLUME, STERILE LEMMA, FERTILE LEMMA
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower glume absent; upper glume and sterile lemma silky-edged; firm fertile lemma inside.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The upper glume is thin, usually 3-veined, and has silky marginal hairs. The lower sterile lemma is similarly thin and can also be hairy; the upper fertile lemma is firm, pale and approximately 1.4–2.6 mm in AusGrass. A source-photographer-annotated reproductive panel labels real organs, but no millimeter ruler is present. Never invent a lower-glume arrow.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL SOURCE-ANNOTATED PARTS — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO MEASURED DISSECTION

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · NO LONG AWN; DALLISGRASS LOOK-ALIKE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Silky glume hairs are NOT awns; dallisgrass often has fewer racemes and larger spikelets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Vaseygrass spikelets commonly measure 2–2.8 mm; Paspalum dilatatum often about 2.7–3.9 mm. These ranges overlap. Compare a full flowering head, measured mature paired spikelets, hairy upper-glume margin and actual collar. Panel 6 is DALLISGRASS, a different species. Johnsongrass instead has a branching panicle with different paired-spikelet architecture.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL DIFFERENT-SPECIES COMPARISON — MATCHED SCALED MATERIAL NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE / PHOTO AND SITE QA
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: three preserved source-labelled photo records; decisive local anatomy remains unverified.
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO (grass photo lane): connected Texas rooted crown, basal sheaths and entire head; same-plant 3–5 mm inner membrane; five mature paired spikelets with 1-mm ruler; 20–40× separated upper glume, sterile lemma, hard fertile lemma and palea; matched P. dilatatum at the same scale. NEEDS_SITE_QA (site lane): verify actual JPEG bytes versus remote-only references, individual Harry Rose CC BY 2.0 credits, original photographer's printed labels, existing gross arrows, comparison species label, all six tiles and mobile/public rendering. Preserve existing taxonomy/range holds and FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until these tests pass; no new photos, arrows or publication claimed.
